title: FontVariation.variation_opentype ignores documented String axis aliases such as "wght"
body:
### Tested Version

master dfa06cafb4

### System Information

Windows 10 Pro, headless, Advanced text server

### Issue Description

The key for the `FontVariation.variation_opentype` dictionary specifies an axis. According to the documentation, the axis can be specified by either a numeric tag or a name (String); it notes that some axes may have multiple names—for instance, `wght` and `weight` refer to the same axis. In reality, however, `weight` works, whereas `wght` does not and is ignored. No error is thrown, and the font remains at its default weight; in short, the key specified in the documentation does not work.

I tested this using the same font, text, and size; the only variable was whether I wrote `weight` or `wght`:
                          wght=100  wght=900
int (tag)  :            117 px         140 px
"weight" :            117 px         140 px
"wght"    :           '130 px'        '130 px'
(no coordinates) :130 px        130 px

The same error exists in three files: the code checks only the numeric tag and the name returned by `tag_to_name()`, without passing String keys through `name_to_tag()`.

Files:
`scene/resources/font.cpp` lines 2419 and 2423
`modules/text_server_adv/text_server_adv.cpp` line 2139
`modules/text_server_fb/text_server_fb.cpp` line 1038

There is an additional consequence: since an unrecognized key is treated as the default in both cases, different values ​​collapse onto the same font RID (the cache returns the same entry).

`editor/themes/editor_fonts.cpp:292` -> uses the "weight" string directly.
`editor/gui/code_editor.cpp:1723` -> converts user input via `name_to_tag()` first.

In other words, advising users to use only the tag is inconsistent with the engine's own code.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached project in Godot once so the font gets imported
2. Run the scene
3. Compare the four printed values

Notes:
This is not a regression; I observed the same issues with 4.6-stable and 4.7-stable as well, though I didn't test them—I only reviewed the code.
I simply examined the code path followed by the importer; I did not compare the on-screen output.

[FontVariation-MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32281468/FontVariation-MRP.zip)
